If you’re going to pay, I would recommend 1Password over LastPass; if not, KeePass is a decent FOSS option (not pretty, but it works).

  • KeePass - Free, opensource, stores your vault locally (sync it yourself with other services)

  • 1Password - $50* for desktop license / free on mobile, proprietary, defaults to storing your vault locally (sync with Dropbox, iCloud, or sync it yourself)

  • LastPass - basic free / $12/year premium, proprietary, defaults to storing your vault on LastPass servers

LastPass has become a big target because they store user vaults. Using it is a little too close to putting all your eggs in one basket, IMO.

*edit: as I write this, 1Password is currently 30% off.
Thanks for the heads up! I was waiting for a good opportunity to buy a 1Password license.
Heh, I wouldn’t have discovered it myself if not for the parent comment. Just upgraded to the multi-OS license.

Isn't storing your vault locally somewhat akin to keeping a text file of your passwords? And wouldn't they still be in one basket? (I'm not actually arguing that LastPass is any better or worse than other password managers.)

Not exactly like a text file. In all cases, the vault is encrypted and locked with a master password.

Hypothetically, if this encryption and your master password are sufficiently strong, it wouldn’t matter where it was stored or who had access to the vault file. You could post it publicly on a website and let anyone download it. Only you would be able to unlock the vault to get the passwords inside.

What I meant about the “one basket” is trusting a single company LastPass at every stage — encrypting the vault, storing the vault on their servers, and keeping the software available on a subscription basis.

LastPass does store your vault locally (the file has to exist somewhere on your disk, and you can read your passwords offline). It just defaults to also syncing with LastPass servers, which I believe can be disabled. I don’t particularly recommend syncing the other password managers’ vaults with Dropbox or iCloud either; the safest is to only store locally on removable media like a USB thumbdrive. Treat it as a physical key that you have to insert in your computer; when you leave your computer your key should go with you, just like how you don’t leave your car or house keys hanging from the door.
